title: 'Share data on river waters': India, China hold 'frank' border talks
content: India and China participated in candid discussions regarding border conditions, taking stock of the current landscape along the Line of Actual Control. New Delhi highlighted the necessity of maintaining peace for the advancement of their bilateral relationship. Furthermore, India sought an expedited meeting on the expert committee for trans-border rivers amidst China's unveiling of a significant dam project upstream.

title: ‘Last time, we failed’: Masked men return to advocate’s house, loot over Rs 3 crore
content: A brazen robbery took place when four masked intruders stormed the home of a senior advocate, threatening him with guns. They escaped with a substantial amount of cash, jewelry worth millions, and a licensed revolver. This residence had already been targeted before. The police are actively investigating by checking city CCTV footage, and security has been intensified around the advocate's dwelling.

title: Why Devdutt Padikkal's fluent ton allows India to breathe easy
content: With Sai Sudharsan all but ruled out of the Sri Lanka series, Devdutt Padikkal seized his chance, scoring a fluent 142 at Colombo’s Nondescript Cricket Club during the warm-up fixture. Displaying assured footwork, confidence against both spin and pace, and solid technique, Padikkal’s performance underscores his readiness for India’s No. 3 spot.

title: ‘Kill my husband or I will’: Man uncovers wife’s chats with lover plotting his murder
content: In a shocking turn of events, a husband has alerted the police about his wife's alleged affair and a potential murder plot. He provided screenshots revealing discussions about orchestrating his murder to resemble a fatal road accident. The police are currently examining the digital evidence's credibility, as both the wife and her accomplice have fled, igniting a manhunt.

title: Mark Zuckerberg gave an update on ‘Meta's 4 am layoff email’ to employees
content: Meta's CEO Mark Zuckerberg addressed the recent layoffs alongside substantial investments in artificial intelligence. Despite reporting impressive revenue growth, the surge in expenses, particularly from severance and legal fees, negatively influenced the second quarter's operating income. The company is committed to advancing its AI infrastructure to pave the way for future innovations and anticipates a reduced headcount due to the layoffs.

title: From training in dry ponds with wooden javelin to following Chopra's trail: Rise of Ashish
content: Ashish secured the second spot in the men's javelin final with a best effort of 74.09 metres, which came in his third attempt. His performance earned India a podium finish at the global junior event. It is the first time India have won a medal in javelin throw at the Junior World Championships since Neeraj Chopra's monster 86.48m showing in 2016.

title: 'Which freedom fighter got most severe punishment?' Kerala probes Savarkar quiz
content: A school quiz question in Kerala has ignited a political controversy. The question asked about the freedom fighter receiving the most severe British punishment. General education minister N Samsudheen ordered an inquiry into the unauthorized quiz. Opposition parties accused the government of promoting a Sangh Parivar agenda. Officials are investigating who prepared and conducted the quiz.

title: Michael Dell’s son’s startup offers $695 alternative to costly home generators
content: Zach Dell's Base Power is installing home battery systems across America.  These systems offer backup power and reduce electricity bills for customers.  The company aims to replace expensive gas generators with its innovative technology.  Base Power is rapidly expanding its operations and customer base nationwide.  This startup is valued at thirteen billion dollars after significant funding.

title: Houston man’s solo trash cleanups grow into 100-volunteer movement
content: A Houston resident's initiative to clean up neglected areas has blossomed into a vibrant volunteer movement. With one hundred dedicated individuals now on board, their mission is to remove illegally dumped waste. Collaborating with local organizations and harnessing the power of social media, city officials and law enforcement are boosting efforts to tackle this pressing issue, ultimately enhancing the community's aesthetics and the well-being of its residents.

title: Billionaire couple offers $150M to make San Francisco better to live in
content: Billionaires Michael Moritz and Harriet Heyman have launched an ambitious $150 million initiative aimed at enhancing San Francisco. Through their foundation, Crankstart, they invite innovative solutions to tackle urgent housing and economic challenges. Organizations can compete for funding, with the evaluation process culminating in a decision set for autumn 2027. This competition highlights the city's increasing dependency on private philanthropy in addressing critical public needs.

title: US proposes ending 60-day grace period for H-1B workers after job loss
content: A US government proposal could eliminate the current 60-day grace period for H-1B visa holders. Affected workers might need to depart the United States immediately after job termination. They generally cannot change immigration status or employers within the country. This rule change applies to several temporary worker visa categories and their dependents. The proposal is currently under federal review and public comment.

title: Chinese grandmother, 71, learns to swim after retirement and saves man
content: A 71-year-old Chinese woman, Liu Defang, saved a man's life after he fell into a river. She had learned to swim only a few years after her retirement from work. Liu bravely entered the water with a lifebuoy to reach the struggling individual. Surveillance footage later revealed her identity, drawing praise from social media users. Her courageous act highlights the value of learning new skills at any age.

title: LeBron James’ wife Savannah reveals why Hermès saleswoman turned her away
content: Savannah James opened up about an alleged Hermès shopping dispute in Italy, claiming a saleswoman was fired after she and April McDaniel were reportedly turned away despite having an appointment. The friends later described how the store addressed the situation. Savannah also discussed marriage, motherhood and life alongside LeBron James, stressing the importance of staying grounded, authentic and invested in a relationship despite the pressure of public life.

title: Dallas Cowboys Cheerleaders’ iconic uniform gets historic update for 2026 NFL season
content: The Dallas Cowboys Cheerleaders will debut a historic update to their iconic uniform during the 2026 NFL season through an expanded partnership with Kendra Scott. The collaboration introduces the first standardized game-day jewelry as part of the squad's look and includes a fan collection inspired by Texas pride. The launch also highlights the growing influence of the cheerleaders beyond football, blending fashion, tradition and modern team branding.

title: 'End this war': Senate Democrats turn up heat on Trump, seek end to Iran hostilities
content: Democrats introduced a resolution to end unauthorized US military involvement against Iran. Senator John Hickenlooper leads the effort, citing constitutional war powers. This move escalates a congressional challenge to President Donald Trump's handling of the conflict. Military leaders privately advise seeking an off-ramp from ongoing air operations. President Trump expresses confidence that the confrontation could end soon.

title: ‘Political drama': DMK skips TVK govt's all-party MP meet on Delimitation Bill
content: The DMK party has officially declared it will not participate in a consultation regarding the delimitation of parliamentary constituencies. Kanimozhi Karunanidhi labeled the meeting organized by the state government as mere political theater. She reiterated the DMK's consistent position on delimitation and called for constitutional changes to uphold the representation of southern states. Additionally, the DMK urged the government to resolve the ongoing Mekedatu dam and Cauvery water disputes.

title: Law grad jumps to death from 13th floor in Bandra after women ‘threatened’ to frame him
content: Police registered a case of abetment of suicide against two women recently. A 24-year-old law graduate died after jumping from his apartment. The women had allegedly threatened to frame him in a police case. This caused the young man significant stress and anxiety. His mother approached Kherwadi Police after the tragic incident.

title: Colorado teen gets $15,000 piano from stranger, releases debut album
content: Colorado teenager Jude Kofie has released his debut album, showcasing his piano skills. He taught himself to play the piano by ear at age ten. A generous piano tuner gifted him a valuable instrument and professional lessons. His album features diverse musical styles, including jazz and gospel influences. This release marks a significant milestone in his developing musical career.

title: Kansas bans student phones, earbuds and smartwatches for entire school day
content: Many states are banning smartphones in schools due to growing distractions and health concerns.  Some districts now restrict student phone access from morning bell to afternoon dismissal.  Parents are increasingly supporting these bans, citing research and developmental appropriateness.  Concerns also focus on excessive screen time and inappropriate content accessed on school devices.  Schools are now reviewing technology policies and limiting device usage during non-instructional periods.

title: Congress lost the millennials. Can it win over Gen Z?
content: Rahul Gandhi is focusing on forging a bond with the youth ahead of the 2029 elections, recognizing that Gen Z will be a key voting bloc.

title: Alliance on the cards? SAD backs Delimitation Bill day after Badal-PM Modi meet
content: Shiromani Akali Dal has expressed strong support for the prompt enactment of the women's reservation bill, emphasizing the need for fair delimitation to ensure equitable state representation. This advocacy follows a meeting between party president Sukhbir Singh Badal and Prime Minister Narendra Modi. Speculation is rife regarding a potential electoral partnership between SAD and BJP, particularly as both parties have faced declining influence in Punjab's political landscape.

title: Sarfaraz Khan in contention to replace Sai Sudharsan for Sri Lanka Tests
content: Sai Sudharsan is all but ruled out of India's Sri Lanka Tests due to a foot niggle, with Shaik Rasheed and Sarfaraz Khan emerging as the frontrunners to replace him. Rasheed's recent India A stint and strong feedback from the CoE could give the youngster the edge.

title: ‘Jealousy, argument, murder’: Classmate slits BCA student’s throat at Lucknow home
content: A tragic incident unfolded when a 20-year-old BCA student was allegedly murdered by her classmate within her own home. The altercation reportedly stemmed from disputes regarding her communication with another individual. Police discovered the victim with severe throat wounds, while the suspect was found injured nearby. Following a confession during the confrontation, the accused has been apprehended, and inquiries continue to ascertain the precise details and motives surrounding this case.

title: 'I've never identified with how I look': 'Musafir Cafe' actress Vedika Pinto
content: Post the humungous success of 'Musafir Cafe', Vedica Pinto gets into a candid chat with Etimes talking about the response to the show co-starring Vikrant Massey, Mahima Makwana, the perceptions about her character Sudha, growing up as an underconfident child, her journey so far from being the 'Liggi' girl to Anurag Kashyap's 'Nishanchi', her aspirations and more. Read on..

title: Why NBFC gold loans are growing nearly 70% despite tighter RBI regulations
content: Non-banking financial company gold loans grew nearly seventy percent year-on-year. This expansion significantly outpaced overall retail credit growth for these institutions. The Reserve Bank of India had introduced new rules for gold lending practices. Despite regulatory scrutiny, demand for gold-backed credit remained robust. Credit growth in industry and services sectors showed moderation during this period.

title: Maharashtra RERA extends timelines for certain projects; here's why it matters
content: In a significant move, Maharashtra's real estate regulator has granted an automatic extension of four months for project completions. Projects originally set to finish on or after February 28, 2026, qualify for this relief. This adjustment acknowledges the global supply chain challenges affecting material availability, which may lead to homebuyers experiencing possession delays of up to four months for their properties.

title: After Germany’s exit, India eyes France-led sixth-generation fighter programme
content: India is discussing joining France's Future Combat Air System program. This development follows Germany's departure from the advanced fighter jet project. India's own fifth-generation fighter is also expected to fly around 2028. This collaboration aligns with India-France's strategic defense partnership goals. The joint effort aims to advance both nations' aerial combat capabilities.

title: Maryland 10-year-old’s champion cake sells for $15,000
content: At a recent county fair auction, a remarkable cake created by 10-year-old baker Herbie Martin IV fetched an astounding $15,000. Herbie dedicated countless late-night hours to master his delightful lemon blueberry recipe. This impressive sale contributed to an overall fundraising goal, raising more than $100,000 for upcoming fairs and youth initiatives, with Herbie's cake standing out as the highlight of the event.

title: 'Congress not realising own errors': Rijiju draws parallel with Indira's post Emergency
content: Parliamentary affairs minister Kiren Rijiju criticized the Congress party for its perceived lack of self-awareness. He contrasted the current leadership with former Prime Minister Indira Gandhi's admission of Emergency actions. Rahul Gandhi questioned the delay in implementing the Women's Reservation Bill. He urged its immediate implementation without linking it to delimitation. The bill's passage and subsequent implementation remain a point of contention.

title: Chitrashi Rawat recalls Shah Rukh Khan as ‘Chak De! India’ turns 19
content: Chitrashi Rawat reflects on her cherished role as Komal Chautala, highlighting a deep bond audiences have with her character. She reminisces about the film's impactful experience, where she formed a close-knit on-screen family. Rawat values the film's enduring messages of unity and resilience, recalling a fond moment with Shah Rukh Khan during filming. She emphasizes how sports serve as a powerful medium for teaching vital life skills.

title: Woman’s skeletal remains found in B'luru home; lived alone after son, husband died
content: In a distressing incident, the skeletal remains of Dakshayini, a 57-year-old woman from Bengaluru, were discovered in her residence. Living independently and suffering from schizophrenia, she had lost touch with her family for nearly two years. The police notified her brother, who confirmed her identity. An unnatural death report is now underway, prompting further investigative actions.

title: Greenland issues ‘strong warning’ over Arctic drilling by Trump-linked firm
content: A US oil firm has moved equipment to Greenland without local approval. This action occurs while President Trump seeks greater US influence over the territory. Greenland's government issued a strong warning regarding the unauthorized logistical operation. The company plans to drill for oil, which faces environmental and political questions. The situation highlights Greenland's resource development authority amid US strategic interests.

title: 'Changing colours like chameleon': Mayawati slams Akhilesh over PDA's 'Pandit' twist
content: BSP chief Mayawati criticized the Samajwadi Party's changing political stance. She accused the SP of altering its PDA formula for electoral gains. Mayawati stated the SP now targets Brahmin voters after noticing BSP's growing support. She urged all communities to remain vigilant against SP's casteist politics. Such deceptive strategies offer short-term benefits but not societal welfare.

title: How US Navy is turning submarines into multi-domain weapons platforms
content: The US Navy is integrating new payload launchers for future attack submarines. These advanced systems will support a wider variety of unmanned systems and payloads. India's Navy is also strengthening its undersea capabilities with new submarine programs. Delays have impacted India's conventional submarine acquisition timeline. Both nations are modernizing their submarine forces for evolving warfare.

title: Estranged wife calls for Gardner's vice-captaincy to be stripped, slams CA
content: Ashleigh Gardner's leadership role faces scrutiny after her estranged wife's public accusations. Monica Wright questioned Cricket Australia's silence regarding the alleged affair with Georgia Voll. Wright believes a power imbalance necessitates consequences for Gardner's leadership position. The Sydney Sixers, however, remain supportive and intend to retain Gardner as captain. This situation highlights Cricket Australia's handling of private matters and workplace responsibilities.

title: Shubman Gill unlikely to bat in warm-up game, on track for Galle Test
content: Shubman Gill, the Indian captain, will miss the warm-up match following a finger injury he picked up during training just a day prior. To prioritise his readiness for the Test, the management has decided that he should take a break. While observing the match from the dugout, Gill also joined in a practice session in the nets.

title: Rude wake-up call, listen to largest voting bloc in 2029: Tharoor on protests
content: Congress MP Shashi Tharoor stressed listening to young people and engaging them.  He noted Gen Z and Gen Alpha will be the largest voting bloc in 2029.  Recent protests and bypoll results showed the growing impact of young voters.  Tharoor believes the ruling party received a wake-up call from these developments.  The Congress party sees opportunities in upcoming state elections next March.
